These facilities support diagnostics and isolated backend development. They are
separate from the numbered analyst-workflow implementation chapters. The normal
Event pipeline uses saved inputs, automatic masks, Stream processing and local
editions as described in articles 11-14.

## Preflight report

`stream_dem_preflight_server()` is an unmounted diagnostic controller. It obtains
a saved request through `store$dem_preflight_request()` and dispatches
`launch_stream_dem_preflight()` to call `fluvgeo::preflight_stream_dem()`.
The report contains grid envelopes, dimensions, storage estimates and source
metadata screening. It allocates no rasters or product files.

The controller distinguishes REVIEW and BLOCKED results, rejects results when
saved requests change, and stops/joins workers on cancellation. Reports are
session snapshots and are not processing approval. See
`fluvgeo/dev/schemas/stream-dem-preflight.md`, `test-stream-dem-preflight.R` and
the backend `test_preflight_stream_dem.R` for the exact diagnostic contract.
Workstation-specific worker setup belongs in the R package development workflow.

## Source annotations

`terrain_source_review_server()` accepts a preflight snapshot and records source
assessment, prior-operation evidence, order and first/last-valid overlap in
immutable JSON annotations. It is not mounted by the analyst app, and the normal
DEM request does not consume these annotations.

`terrain_review_binding`, `terrain_review_write` and `terrain_review_latest` bind
records to checked inputs, validate rows/order and protect concurrent saves with
an exclusive lock and rename. Changed snapshots invalidate drafts. The store
adapters are `terrain_review` and `save_terrain_review`. Notes neither change
rasters nor clear grid/reference incompatibilities. The schema is
`dev/schemas/terrain-source-review.md`; tests are `test-terrain-source-review.R`.

## Horizontal warp API

`fluvgeo::warp_terrain_horizontal()` takes a source GeoTIFF, an output-grid template
and a new output directory. It has no FG Studio pipeline caller. Template values
are not an analysis mask. The API uses GDAL with an explicit horizontal pipeline
and `-novshift` to preserve elevation units and source vertical evidence.

Aligned grids use nearest sampling; other grids use bilinear interpolation.
Float32 is the default storage type, with explicit Float64 support. GDAL manages
working precision; terra supplies native summaries. Analytical warping uses base
pixels. The operation supports north-up targets and static east/north projected
CRSs with the same identified geodetic base. Datum/epoch changes, nonidentity
scale/offset and external georeferencing/mask sidecars are outside this API's
supported profile.

See fluvgeo `R/warp_terrain_horizontal.R`, `test_warp_terrain_horizontal.R` and
`dev/schemas/horizontal-terrain-warp.md`. These define the API independently of
whether it is integrated into the Stream DEM workflow.

## Bounded development targets

`fgstudio.dem_reach` or `fgstudio.dem_stream` targets one saved record for isolated
processing. `fgstudio.mosaic_trial` supplies a real-window diagnostic fixture.
These options are not needed by normal sessions. Use small subsets of actual
downloaded DEMs for function trials and parameter checks, following
`dev/workflows/r-spatial.md`.

`fgstudio.mask_diagnostics=TRUE` enables optional mask inspection. Display products
are prepared in the worker and cached for the session; the selector changes only
the viewed result. This development facility is disabled by default. Analytical
mask generation is independent of its display.
